title: Clean Claims: What They Are and Why They Matter
summary: A clean claim contains all required data elements and passes payer edits on first submission — the foundation of an efficient revenue cycle.
objectives: Define a clean claim and its required data elements
Describe the claim editing process and common rejection reasons
Explain the financial impact of clean claim rate on overall RCM performance

content_blocks.body:
A clean claim is one that:
- Contains all required demographic and insurance information
- Has valid diagnosis (ICD-10-CM) and procedure (CPT/HCPCS) codes
- Includes a valid NPI for the billing and rendering provider
- Has the correct revenue codes (for institutional claims)
- Passes all payer-specific edits and HIPAA transaction standards
- Is submitted within the payer's timely filing deadline

Clean claim rates of 95%+ are the industry benchmark; top performers achieve 98–99%.
content_blocks.heading: What Makes a Claim 'Clean'?

content_blocks.body: A **rejection** occurs before the claim is processed — the claim fails edits and is returned without adjudication. Rejections can be corrected and resubmitted. A **denial** occurs after the claim is processed — the payer adjudicates the claim but refuses payment. Denials require an appeal and formal dispute process. Tracking these separately is essential for root cause analysis.
content_blocks.title: Rejection vs. Denial: A Critical Distinction
